name_reason: Current name has a redundant doubled domain token: convention is data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with domain=chapter, but the descriptor re-prepends 'chapter' yielding the awkward '...chapter_chapter_init_done_flag'. Dropping the duplicate gives data_fd2_chapter_init_done_flag (domain chapter + descriptor init_done_flag). The descriptor still reflects the data type (a flag). Not an address residue and not a domain ID -- pure redundancy. No collision with the sibling global data_fd2_chapter_init_phase_flag (distinct descriptor). Rename only RECORDED here; applied in Stage 2 across globals.h/protos.h/call sites.
purpose: Single-byte runtime state flag that latches the one-time transition out of chapter init into active gameplay.
logic_summary: BSS zero at program load. fd2_set_chapter_init_done_flag @ 0x33FB9 unconditionally stores 1 (MOV byte [0x53A44],1; verified by disassembly -- no other side effects). fd2_game_main_loop @ 0x118A3 reads it byte-wide in the action/confirm (Space 0x39 / Enter 0x1C) path as `while (flag == 0) fd2_set_chapter_init_done_flag();`, but only when data_fd2_ui_click_debounce_skip_count == 0. Because the setter always writes 1, the loop body executes exactly once, latching the flag 0 -> 1 on the first qualifying confirm; later confirms skip the spin. Exactly one reader and one writer (verified by xrefs).
element_semantics: Boolean latch: 0 = chapter init not yet completed; 1 = init done / gameplay active. Accessed byte-wide only.
notes: is_const=false confirmed by the game-side write-xref at 0x33FB9. read_memory shows all-zero (BSS/tentative). MNEMONIC=undefined1 confirms 1-byte width. src comment block (lines 494-502) is already accurate/precise/ASCII and consistent with the Ghidra plate, so comment kept; it retains the current live name on purpose (rename deferred to Stage 2 to stay in sync with the still-current declaration). Ghidra plate is detailed and non-contradictory -> left untouched. Adjacent global data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr @ 0x53A45 (4-byte pointer) is a distinct neighbor, not an overlap; byte-wide accesses do not touch it. No src edits this round (comment kept, rename only recorded).
